chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah al-Ash'ari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers (peace be upon them).
He said: Separate the beds of the boys from those of the women when they reach ten years of age.
ai.seo_question: At what age should children be separated from women in their sleeping arrangements according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes the age of ten (‘ashariyyun) as the threshold for modesty (hijab) in domestic settings, a ruling widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as the point when children become accountable for basic privacy norms. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on gradual socialization into gender segregation, ensuring that the transition to adult modesty is structured and age-appropriate within the family unit.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-30 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qad’dah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), “
You should separate the beds of boys from that of other women when they become ten years old.”
